findings.claim: SNF level-of-care is a covered category, but it requires a daily skilled service. Intermittent skilled need would not qualify, and the facts do not settle whether the daily skilled need was met.
findings.quote: payment for a SNF level of care could not be made if a patient needs an intermittent rather than daily skilled service
findings.case_fact: For example, payment for a SNF level of care could not be made if a patient needs an intermittent rather than daily skilled service.

findings.claim: Coverage turns first on whether a skilled need exists. The contractor found no documentation of daily skilled nursing, and the therapy was found not reasonable and necessary, so the basic skilled-care eligibility condition is unresolved or disputed.
findings.quote: the A/B MAC (A) first considers whether a patient needs skilled care
findings.case_fact: after finding that the record did not contain documentation to support a finding for medically reasonable and necessary daily SN services.

findings.quote: The beneficiary must meet technical eligibility requirements (e.g., a 3-day hospital stay, etc.)
findings.case_fact: hospital records concerning the beneficiary’s December 15, 2009, through December 27, 2009, stay at *** *** Hospital.

findings.case_fact: On at least thirteen occasions the beneficiary’s medications had to be adjusted due to fluctuations in his blood pressure and heart rate.

findings.claim: UNKNOWN: the facts do not show whether the SNF admission followed the hospital discharge directly or within 30 days. They also do not show physician certification. findings.claim: The policy covers inpatient hospital care only where hospitalization is needed. Here the QIC found the documentation does not support the medical necessity of the acute inpatient stays, so the basic inpatient-eligibility condition is not shown to be met.
findings.quote: If care is noncovered because a patient does not need to be hospitalized, the A/B MAC Part A denies the admission
findings.case_fact: the medical documentation in each case does not support the medical necessity for the acute hospitalizations.

findings.claim: Patient status (inpatient vs. outpatient) is the threshold question. The RAC found the services belonged in an outpatient setting. findings.quote: expected to keep them in the hospital for only a few hours (less than 24), they are considered outpatients for coverage purposes
findings.case_fact: determined that the services should have been provided to the beneficiaries in an outpatient setting

findings.claim: The case facts describe only a procedural matter (a late request for an extension of time to file an appellant's brief). They say nothing about a SNF service, hospital stay, transfer timing, or skilled care, so the passage's technical eligibility requirements cannot be assessed.
findings.quote: The beneficiary must meet technical eligibility requirements (e.g., a 3-day hospital stay, etc.), services must be reasonable and necessary
findings.case_fact: the appellant filed, by telefacsimile, a request for an additional extension of time, to January 10, 2010, to brief the case.

findings.claim: The policy covers post-hospital extended care that follows a qualifying inpatient stay. The case facts give no hospital stay, discharge date, or SNF admission, so the 3-day stay and 30-day transfer conditions cannot be confirmed or refuted.
findings.quote: the individual must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least three consecutive calendar days.
findings.case_fact: The appellant’s brief was received after January 10, 2010, by telefacsimile.

findings.claim: The beneficiary was admitted to the SNF after a hospital stay described as qualifying, which meets the prior-hospitalization eligibility condition. The 3-day length is not stated in the facts and relies on the 'qualifying' label.

findings.case_fact: admitted to *** skilled nursing facility (SNF) on January 17, 2006, after a qualifying hospital stay for treatment of delirium

findings.case_fact: The beneficiary received skilled physical and occupational therapies after admission.

findings.case_fact: admitted to *** skilled nursing facility (SNF) on January 17, 2006, after a qualifying hospital stay for treatment of delirium

findings.case_fact: had a primary diagnosis of cerebrovascular accident complications

findings.claim: Living in an assisted living facility does not bar home health coverage, but coverage depends on the facility not being primarily engaged in providing medical or skilled care. The record does not say what kind of facility this is.
findings.quote: Medicare will cover reasonable and necessary home health care furnished to these individuals
findings.case_fact: resided in an assisted living facility

findings.quote: If the patient does in fact leave the home, the patient may nevertheless be considered homebound if the absences from the home are infrequent
findings.case_fact: It is unclear whether the beneficiary merely left his personal room or the entire facility.

findings.claim: The case facts do not show that a physician or allowed practitioner certified that the beneficiary is confined to the home. The only related fact is the appellant's argument about the Plans of Care, so certification is UNKNOWN.
findings.quote: the law requires that a physician or allowed practitioner certify in all cases that the patient is confined to his/her home
findings.case_fact: Appellant argues that the Plans of Care and the record as a whole support a finding that beneficiary was “confined to the home.”

findings.claim: The policy first requires a need for skilled care before SNF level-of-care payment can be considered. The case facts say the resident would no longer require skilled care, so this basic eligibility condition does not appear met.
findings.quote: first considers whether a patient needs skilled care
findings.case_fact: Resident will no longer require skilled care

findings.claim: The beneficiary was in hospice during the billed dates. Hospice-SNF services for the terminal condition are handled by the hospice contract, not billed to the A/B MAC. This is consistent with the denial of the SNF claims.
findings.quote: Hospices contract with SNFs for services related to the beneficiary’s terminal condition.
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary was receiving Medicare-covered hospice services on the dates of service in question

findings.claim: SNF PPS payment for a hospice patient is possible only for daily skilled care unrelated to the terminal condition. The case facts do not show any such unrelated skilled need, so this exception is not established (UNKNOWN).
findings.quote: later requires daily skilled care unrelated to the terminal condition
findings.case_fact: The appellant later signed a hospice election for the beneficiary on January 28, 2009.

findings.claim: Skilled nursing visits to manage a diabetic patient's medication regimen are a type of home health service the policy recognizes as covered.
findings.quote: skilled nursing visits for teaching of self-administration and self- management of the medication regimen
findings.case_fact: New England Home Care provided home health services (nursing visits) to the beneficiary, who has diabetes and is legally blind.

findings.claim: The policy says skilled care can remain necessary when a patient is stable. The nursing visits therefore are not excluded merely because the patient's condition is stable or chronic.
findings.quote: Skilled care may, depending on the unique condition of the patient, continue to be necessary for patients whose condition is stable.
findings.case_fact: skilled care may, depending on the unique condition of the patient, continue to be necessary for patients whose condition is stable.

findings.case_fact: Moreover, the records dated within this period include numerous documented instances of changes in the beneficiary’s medication schedule,

findings.claim: UNKNOWN: the passages and case facts do not settle homebound status, physician certification, or the plan of care. The record only shows that the contractor allowed part of the period, so these basic conditions cannot be confirmed.
findings.quote: A physician has ordered skilled nursing visits
findings.case_fact: allowed coverage for the home health nursing visits provided from May 28, 2008 to June 20, 2008

findings.quote: Such signs and symptoms as abnormal/fluctuating vital signs, weight changes, edema, symptoms of drug toxicity, abnormal/fluctuating lab values
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary required and received daily skilled nursing services in the form of skilled observation and assessment

findings.claim: Eligibility turns first on whether the patient needs skilled care. The case facts say nothing about the patient's condition, the services received, daily need, or SNF stay status, so these basic conditions cannot be confirmed.

findings.case_fact: The Jimmo v. Sebelius Settlement Agreement Fact Sheet is not itself authority, but it concisely restates the governing coverage standards

findings.case_fact: Beneficiary J.S. Issues: SNF Coverage (Part A) Dates of Service: September 1-18, 2008

findings.quote: first considers whether a patient needs skilled care
findings.case_fact: That is, there is no evidence that the performance of the services provided necessitated skilled professionals.

findings.claim: Skilled nursing for Lupron injections every 90 days is a type of care the policy addresses. findings.quote: the Medicare contractor should evaluate each claim involving skilled nursing services furnished less frequently than once every 60 days.

findings.claim: Physical therapy for gait and stair training in a patient with impaired walking from a skeletal abnormality is a covered type of skilled PT under the gait training provision.

findings.case_fact: a skeletal abnormality of uneven leg length further interfering with his ability to ambulate

findings.quote: Physical therapy would be reasonable and necessary to teach the patient to climb and descend stairs safely.
findings.case_fact: the skilled therapist was needed to teach the beneficiary how to safely transfer to and from the lift.

findings.quote: Teaching wound care where the complexity of the wound, the overall condition of the patient or the ability of the caregiver makes teaching necessary

findings.case_fact: home health aide visits ranging between five and seven days per week, and between four and 24 hours per day

findings.quote: The documentation that IRFs are already required to complete to meet the IRF coverage requirements

findings.quote: may be used to satisfy the certification and recertification statement requirements

findings.case_fact: On July 27, 2009, the beneficiary was admitted to Twin Maples Health Care Facility, the appellant’s SNF.

findings.quote: The patient requires these skilled services on a daily basis
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary also required and received skilled nursing services for other medical needs, apparently not related to her psychiatric diagnoses.

findings.case_fact: ambulate 250 feet modified independent with front wheeled walker

findings.case_fact: The beneficiary was seen at the IRF by at least three physicians and was monitored daily by the nursing staff.
